title: Policy in Relation to Share Trading

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of the Company, and for the purposes of this Policy includes the Chief Executive Officer. Subject to the hedging ban in 4.3, margin lending consent in section 5, and clearance from the Chairman and one Authorised Person.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Director appointed Chairman of the Board. Distinguished only because his or her own dealing clearance and margin lending consent are escalated to the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee or Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Relevant Employee
tiers.description: An employee of the Company; a director or employee of a related body corporate; or a contractor providing services similar to an employee under a contract exceeding 6 months. Subject to general clearance from two Authorised Persons but not to the section 5 margin lending consent regime, which is limited to Directors and GDG's Executive Team.

tiers.name: GDG's Executive Team
tiers.description: Referenced in paragraphs 4.2 and 5.1-5.2 alongside Directors for the no-inside-information declaration and the margin lending/secured financing consent requirement; not separately defined in the Policy and presumably a subset of Relevant Employees.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Has the same meaning as in section 9 of the Corporations Act 2001 and includes a person's spouse, defacto, family members, controlled trusts and companies, or other third parties contemplating the acquisition or sale of securities on behalf of the person.

tiers.name: Investment Managers
tiers.description: A person who manages investments (whether or not on a discretionary basis) on behalf of a Director or Relevant Employee or their Associates, excluding managers of interests in a registered managed investment scheme.

rules.detail: Securities is defined narrowly as listed or unlisted shares, debentures, interests, rights, units or option contracts in the Company, so a bank-written OTC put/call is not itself 'Securities'. However Dealing includes 'entering into any other form of agreement to acquire or dispose of an interest in securities', which arguably catches entering a derivative referencing those shares; on that basis the general clearance requirement in paragraph 6 applies.
rules.evidence: "Dealing" includes ... entering into any other form of agreement to acquire or dispose of an interest in securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on a Director hedging exposure to an unvested option.
rules.evidence: A Director must not enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge his or her exposure to ... an unvested option.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on a Director hedging exposure to a Security subject to retention arrangements (a vested but locked/escrowed holding).
rules.evidence: A Director must not enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge his or her exposure to: (1) a Security that is subject to retention arrangements.

rules.detail: The express hedging ban is limited to retention-locked securities and unvested options; hedging of vested, unrestricted Director shares is not named and falls back to the general Dealing clearance regime.
rules.evidence: A Director must not enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge his or her exposure to: (1) a Security that is subject to retention arrangements; or (2) an unvested option.

rules.detail: The paragraph 4.3 hedging ban applies only to Directors; hedging by a Relevant Employee is not named and is caught only via the general Dealing clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: A Relevant Employee must not deal in Securities without obtaining the prior approval of two Authorised Persons.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward sale) is not named; it is caught as an agreement to acquire or dispose of an interest in securities, requiring the general clearance under paragraph 6.
rules.evidence: "Dealing" includes any subscription, redemption, purchase or sale of securities, or any agreement to effect the same.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named in the Policy and is not listed among the guidance items in paragraph 13.1.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named; treated the same as other derivative agreements referencing an interest in securities and so subject to the general clearance requirement, though the narrow Securities definition leaves this uncertain.

financing_disclosure: Directors and GDG's Executive Team: if required by the Company, provide the Company Secretary with information relevant to the margin loan or financing arrangement; no fixed trigger or deadline stated (5.2).

exemption_authority: The person responsible for giving clearance may permit a sale (not a purchase) during a closed period in exceptional circumstances, such as a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied, provided no other prohibition applies (paragraphs 10.1-10.3). No exemption exists for the margin lending/secured financing consent regime in section 5.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A 'significant holding' of Company securities is a holding of more than 1% of the issued capital of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The section 5 consent requirement for margin loans and other secured financing is only triggered once the collared shares (together with other holdings) exceed 1% of issued capital; a collar over a smaller stake may fall outside that consent requirement on the plain wording.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy continues to apply to all Directors and members of GDG's Executive Team regardless of commitments which such individuals may enter into in relation to margin lending contracts or other financing arrangements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A lender's contractual right to force a sale on default does not override the Policy; enforcement or physical settlement during a closed period or while holding inside information would still need to satisfy the ordinary dealing/clearance rules, creating execution risk for the bank's security.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Director must not enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge his or her exposure to: (1) a Security that is subject to retention arrangements; or (2) an unvested option.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted director shares (no longer subject to retention/escrow) is not caught by this express hedging ban; it would block a collar only over retention-locked or unvested holdings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairman must not deal in Securities without obtaining the prior approval of either the Chair of the Remuneration and Nomination Committee or Chair of the Audit Committee and one Authorised Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the counterparty director is the Chairman, sign-off for the collar and any secured loan routes to board committee chairs rather than the Chairman personally, adding an approval step.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of GDG's Executive Team must make a declaration to the effect that they are not in possession of any unpublished price sensitive information when seeking approval to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar execution, and any later unwind or roll (each a fresh Dealing requiring fresh clearance), requires a fresh no-inside-information declaration each time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings in Securities must be completed within 1 month of approval being granted, unless otherwise advised by the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (and its secured loan) must be priced and executed within roughly 30 days of clearance or a fresh approval will be needed.

summary: A funded collar is arguably possible under this policy, though it is not squarely addressed. Because 'Securities' is defined narrowly as Company-issued shares, debentures, rights, units or options, an OTC put/call written by a bank is not itself 'Securities', but entering into it is likely still a 'Dealing' (an agreement to acquire or dispose of an interest in securities) requiring ordinary clearance -- Chairman and one Authorised Person for Directors, two Authorised Persons for other Relevant Employees -- outside closed periods and while not holding inside information. The loan leg secured on the collared shares falls within section 5: Directors and GDG's Executive Team need prior Chairman consent (Audit Committee Chair consent if the Chairman is the borrower) only once the secured holding exceeds 1% of issued capital; below that threshold, or for an ordinary Relevant Employee, the policy does not address secured financing at all. The paragraph 4.3 hedging ban only stops a Director hedging retention-locked or unvested holdings, so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares escapes it. Key execution risks are the roughly 30-day validity of any clearance and the requirement to re-declare no inside information for entry, unwind, or roll, since the policy expressly continues to bind the executive regardless of financing commitments made to a lender.
